explain.say: What happens to your old phone when you get a new one? Often it ends up in a drawer or a dump. But what if nothing was ever wasted? Look at the board: a circle where things are made, used, fixed and remade.

explain.say: First, see the old way: a straight line. Take raw materials, make a product, use it, throw it away. Economists call this a linear economy. Materials run out at one end and waste piles up at the other. Can you see the problem?

stages.label: Use
stages.note: Use it for a short time.

explain.say: Now the circle. It starts with design to last: making things easy to repair and take apart. A phone with a battery you can swap lasts years longer. What thing in your home breaks too easily?

explain.say: Look at repair and reuse. In India, street repair stalls fix phones and fans for a small fee, and in Ghana and Nigeria skilled technicians refurbish old electronics. Fixing keeps value in use. Have you ever had something repaired?

faq.a: It is an economy designed to keep products and materials in use for as long as possible, by designing for repair, sharing, reusing and recycling, instead of throwing things away.
A linear economy follows take, make, use, throw away. It uses up raw materials and creates lots of waste.
If ten neighbours share one drill or one car, far fewer need to be made. Libraries, tool libraries, bike-share schemes and rental apps all save materials.

faq.q: What is the right to repair?
faq.a: It is the idea that people should be able to fix their own products, with spare parts and repair guides available. The European Union passed right-to-repair rules in 2024.
asks: Why can't I fix my phone?

faq.a: Recycling helps, but it uses energy and some materials cannot be recycled well. Using less, repairing and reusing come first; recycling is the last step in the loop.

facts: The Global E-waste Monitor 2024 reported 62 million tonnes of e-waste in 2022, with about 22 percent documented as properly recycled.
The European Union adopted right-to-repair rules for many consumer products in 2024.
